test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following organ is part of excretory system in human human body? 

I. A pair of ureters

II. A urethra
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The human excretory system** is responsible for the elimination of metabolic waste products and toxins from the body, ensuring homeostasis.
 
• **Statement I: A pair of ureters** – Ureters are part of the excretory system. They are two tubes that transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Statement II: A urethra** – The urethra is also part of the excretory system. It is a tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body during urination. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Both **ureters** and the **urethra** play key roles in the proper functioning of the urinary system, which is a crucial component of the excretory system.
 
• As both statements are correct, the correct answer is **Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of the human excretory system:**

 
 
• The system consists of the **kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra**.
 
• The **kidneys** filter blood to remove waste products and excess substances, forming urine.
 
• The **ureters** are muscular tubes that transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.
 
• The **urinary bladder** stores urine temporarily until it is expelled from the body.
 
• The **urethra** is the final part of the system that allows urine to exit the body.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the excretory system:**
 
 
• Regulation of water and electrolyte balance in the body.
 
• Removal of metabolic waste products like urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
 
• Detoxification of harmful substances.
 
• Maintaining blood pressure and pH levels.
 
 
 
• **Diseases related to the excretory system:**
 
 
• **Kidney stones:** Hard deposits of minerals and salts that can obstruct the urinary flow.
 
• **Urinary tract infections (UTIs):** Infections in the urinary system caused by bacteria.
 
• **Chronic kidney disease:** Gradual loss of kidney function over time.
 
 
 
• **Importance of hydration:** Drinking sufficient water aids in the efficient functioning of the excretory system and prevents conditions like kidney stones and UTIs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the ureters:** Ureters are approximately 25–30 cm long and use peristaltic movements to transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
 
• **Role of the urethra:** The length of the urethra varies between males and females. In males, it also serves as a passage for semen during reproduction.
 
• **Excretion vs. Egestion:** Excretion refers to the removal of metabolic waste, whereas egestion involves the elimination of undigested food residue from the digestive system.
 
• **Clinical relevance:** Diagnostic tools like urinalysis and imaging techniques (e.g., ultrasounds) are used to assess the health of the excretory system.
